dialogue.text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me when your dizziness first started and if it comes in brief episodes or lasts for a long time?
It started just this morning, and it hasn't really stopped since then. It feels like the room is constantly spinning, though the sensation is somewhat low grade.
Have you noticed any changes in your hearing or any ringing in your ears since this started? I'd also like to know if you're experiencing any headache or neck pain.
No, my hearing seems fine and I haven't noticed any ringing or ear pain. I don't really have a headache or neck pain either, just this constant spinning and some nausea.
Have you recently had a cold, the flu, or any other viral infection in the past few weeks? Also, are you experiencing any double vision, numbness, or weakness in your arms or legs?

I actually did have a cold a few days ago, which is why I've been eating a lot of extra garlic to try and get over it. I don't have any double vision or weakness in my limbs, though. Everything feels normal except for this spinning sensation.
Does the spinning sensation change or get worse when you move your head or change positions? I would also like to check for any involuntary eye movements. REQUEST TEST: Nystagmus_Test
RESULTS: Nystagmus noted.

Since the room is spinning, does the intensity change at all when you move your head, or is it truly constant? I'd like to perform a quick test on your eye movements while I move your head. REQUEST TEST: Head_Impulse_Test
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
I'm going to check if your eyes are vertically misaligned. REQUEST TEST: Test_of_Skew. How steady are you on your feet when you try to walk?
dialogue.payload: Test_of_Skew. How steady are you on your feet when you try to walk?

I see, that sounds a bit serious. What exactly are you looking for in my eyes, and is there anything else I should be doing while you check them? My vision just feels so "jumpy" whenever I try to look around the room.
I am looking to see if the direction of your eye jumping changes when you look to the left versus the right, which helps me determine if this is an inner ear issue or something related to the brain

That makes sense, I just want this spinning to stop so I can feel steady again. I'm trying to keep my head still for you, but even looking to the side makes me feel even more nauseous. Do you think the diphenhydramine I took earlier is making it harder for you to see what my eyes are doing?
Yes, diphenhydramine can dampen the eye movements, but I can still see the nystagmus clearly. Does the "jumping" in your eyes always move in the same direction, or

It seems like they are always jumping in the same direction, no matter which way I try to look. It’s just a constant, rhythmic pulling sensation that won't let up. Does that help you figure out what's going on with me?

That is helpful information, as unidirectional nystagmus is often seen with inner ear issues. However, since your Head Impulse Test was normal despite the constant spinning, I need to rule out more serious causes

That sounds a bit concerning—what serious causes are you thinking of? I was really hoping it was just a lingering effect from my cold or maybe all that garlic I've been eating. Is there another test we need to do to be sure?

A stroke? That’s really scary to hear at my age, especially since I'm usually so healthy. Please, tell me what I need to do for the coordination check so we can figure this out.
I understand this is worrying, but we need to be very thorough to get you the right care. Please try to touch your nose and then my finger as accurately as you can. REQUEST TEST: Finger_to_Nose_Test
RESULTS: NORMAL READINGS
Your coordination looks good, which is a positive sign. I'd like to check your balance more closely—could you try to stand with your feet together and eyes closed? REQUEST TEST: Romberg
RESULTS: Unstable tandem gait but unremarkable baseline gait. Patient reports sensation of imbalance.

I understand, but please tell me more about what those results mean for me. If my coordination and walking aren't quite right, does that point back to the stroke you mentioned? I’m just feeling very anxious and dizzy right now.
I'll do my best to explain. While your coordination is good, a normal Head Impulse Test in someone with constant spinning can actually be a sign that the problem is in the

If the problem is in the brain, does that mean I'll need a scan or something to see what's happening? I'm just really confused because I felt fine until this morning, other than that cold I had. Please, just tell me what the next step is to get this spinning under control.

We can certainly provide some anti-nausea medication to help you feel more comfortable while we proceed. I would like to order one final imaging test to be absolutely certain about what's happening. REQUEST TEST
RESULTS: No acute abnormalities noted, specifically no signs of stroke or significant lesions.

The MRI results show no signs of a stroke or other abnormalities in the brain, which is very reassuring news. Given the constant spinning and the fact that it started after a cold, it appears the viral

That is such a relief to hear, because I was honestly terrified when you mentioned a stroke. So, if it's not my brain, does this mean the cold I had just moved into my inner ear? I really hope there's a way to make this spinning stop soon.
